items.definition:
distance north or south of the equator
The city is located at a high latitude.

comprehensive knowledge or skill
Achieving mastery in a language takes years of practice.

excessive dose of a drug
He was rushed to the hospital after an overdose.

group moving in an orderly way
The funeral procession moved slowly down the street.

act of moving to a new place
The company offered a relocation package to its employees.

great wealth or valuable possessions
He inherited vast riches from his ancestors.

type of rock
The ancient temple was built from red sandstone.

public health conditions related to clean water and waste disposal
Improved sanitation is crucial for preventing disease.

the state of being kept secret
The project was shrouded in secrecy.

a device that changes voltage; a robot that can change form
The electrical transformer hummed loudly.

poisonous fluid secreted by animals
The snake injected its venom into the mouse.

the state of being in good health
The company promotes employee wellness programs.

a player in a wing position in sports
The winger scored a brilliant goal.

the part of the body containing the digestive organs
He felt a pain in his abdomen.

a small rocky body orbiting the sun
Scientists are tracking a large asteroid.

something that increases strength or effectiveness
He received a booster shot for the vaccine.

the state of being imprisoned or confined
The animal spent its entire life in captivity.

an event causing great and often sudden damage or suffering; a disaster
The earthquake was a complete catastrophe for the region.

the state of being connected or interconnected
The hotel offers free Wi-Fi connectivity for guests.

a person who is very interested in a particular activity or subject
He is a keen car enthusiast.

a burial ground, especially one beside a church
The old church had a small graveyard next to it.

severe suffering or privation
The family faced many hardships during the war.

lack of confidence or safety
His insecurity made him hesitant to speak in public.

the act of questioning someone thoroughly
The suspect underwent a long interrogation at the police station.

the use of various media, such as text, audio, and video
The presentation included a lot of multimedia elements, like videos and sound clips.

a person who does not belong to a particular group or society
He felt like an outsider in the new school.

a person or company that organizes or finances an event or product
The concert promoter announced the new tour dates.

a sacred song or poem, especially one from the Book of Psalms
She read a psalm from the Bible during the service.

a change to an opposite direction, position, or course of action
The team suffered a sudden reversal of fortune.

a period of unrestrained activity of a particular kind
She went on a shopping spree after getting her bonus.

a person with an interest or concern in something, especially a business
All stakeholders were invited to the meeting to discuss the project.

a violent person, especially a criminal
The police arrested the thug for assault.

the quality of being arrogant
His arrogance made him unpopular with his colleagues.

an Australian (informal)
My friend is an Aussie who loves surfing.

a Christian sacrament
The baby's baptism took place last Sunday.

a man (informal British English)
He's a good bloke, always willing to help.

a person who books performers or events
The concert booker arranged for the band to play next month.

forehead; the top of a hill
He wiped the sweat from his brow.

a large bowl-shaped cavity in the ground or on a celestial body
The meteor left a huge crater when it hit the ground.

a keeper or custodian of a museum or other collection
The museum curator was responsible for the new exhibition.

a state of despair, typically one which results in rash or extreme behavior
In desperation, he tried one last time to open the locked door.

a condition in which feces are discharged from the bowels frequently and in a liquid form
He had severe diarrhea after eating the spoiled food.

a small seed-eating songbird
A small finch landed on the bird feeder.

a member of a gang of criminals
The movie was about a notorious gangster from the 1930s.

something that is given free, often for promotional purposes
The company offered a free giveaway to attract new customers.

the action of humiliating someone or the state of being humiliated
He felt deep humiliation after his public mistake.

Master of Business Administration
She decided to pursue an MBA to advance her career.

complete failure; emotional collapse
The stock market experienced a complete meltdown after the news.

an obstacle or blockage
There was an obstruction on the road, causing a delay.

the way someone or something is represented or described
The movie's portrayal of the historical event was very accurate.

a joke exploiting the different possible meanings of a word or the fact that there are words which sound alike but have different meanings
He made a clever pun about the baker, saying he kneaded dough.

a measure taken to protect something or someone
The new laws provide a safeguard against discrimination.

waste water
The city's sewage system needs an upgrade.

informal language
It's hard to understand all the local slang.

information that reveals the plot of a story
Don't tell me the ending, no spoilers!

a pub or inn
We stopped at the old tavern for a drink.

a message sent by telegraph
In the past, important news was often sent by telegram.

a strong, light metal
The aircraft parts were made of titanium.

violent or unsteady movement of air or water
The plane experienced some turbulence during the flight.

the quality of being urgent
The message was delivered with great urgency.

articles of a particular type, typically those sold in a shop
The store sells various kinds of kitchenware.

the choice and arrangement of words
The wording of the contract was very precise.

a change or modification
The tailor made an alteration to the dress.

the action of keeping away from or preventing something
His avoidance of eye contact made her suspicious.
